learningObjective: Explain the semantics of warps, blocks and grids in CUDA and the resources they share.
stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship among threads, warps, blocks and grids on NVIDIA GPUs (compute capability 8.0)?

options.text: A warp is a group of 32 threads that share a warp scheduler and are always drawn from the same block; a block is assigned to a single SM and its threads share shared memory and __syncthreads() barrier; a grid spans many blocks that may run on different SMs and cannot rely on cross-block barriers without cooperative-groups grid sync.
A warp of 32 threads is scheduled independently and may be composed of threads from different thread blocks to improve occupancy when a single block cannot fill an SM.
All blocks in a grid share a single shared-memory bank because shared memory is L1-cached across SMs, providing a form of grid-level synchronization.
Grid-level synchronization is implicit at every kernel launch boundary; __syncthreads() therefore synchronizes all threads across the entire grid.

explanation: A: The CUDA execution model defines a warp as 32 threads from a single block, scheduled together on one SM warp scheduler. A block is assigned to exactly one SM; block-scope shared memory and __syncthreads() operate within that block. Cross-block synchronization within a grid requires cooperative groups (grid.sync()) with grid-launch support. B is false — warps are not composed across blocks. C is false — shared memory is per-SM and per-block; there is no cross-SM shared bank. D is false — __syncthreads() is a block-scope barrier, not grid-scope.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: warps are within a block, blocks run on one SM, grid spans SMs, cross-block sync needs cooperative groups.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: a warp cannot mix threads from different blocks.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: shared memory is per-block; there is no cross-SM shared-memory bank.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: __syncthreads() is block-scope; grid-level barriers require grid.sync() with cooperative launch.

assumptions: NVIDIA Ampere or later; warp size 32.
Standard (non-cooperative) kernel launch semantics for the __syncthreads() claim.
nonImplications: Does not imply blocks are always resident concurrently on an SM; some blocks queue and become resident as prior ones finish.
Does not imply cooperative launch is always possible — it requires all blocks to fit resident on the GPU simultaneously.

distractorRationales.C: Confuses per-block shared memory with global L2/L1 caches.
